findings.note: An exported METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL or METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT breaks `fsm init` for any workflow that does not declare a JUDGE / JUDGE_EFFORT var. applyJudgeOverrideFor (internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:276-289) writes out[JudgeVar]/out[JudgeEffortVar] whenever the override is non-empty, with no check that the target workflow declares those vars, and workflow.Resolve refuses any undeclared var. Reproduced with the built binary in a scratch repo against a custom path workflow declaring only REVIEWER and REV_EFFORT: with no env the init succeeds (status OK, workflow_source path); with METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL=gpt-5.2 exported the same command fails ERR_VAR_UNKNOWN {"name":"JUDGE"} ("unknown var JUDGE"), and METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT alone fails the same way on JUDGE_EFFORT. This is exactly the failure class the sibling calibration rule at wiring.go:258-266 was written to prevent ("exporting METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL once would otherwise make every later calibration run fail ... naming a flag the operator never passed"), and the error names a var the operator never passed, giving no hint that an ambient environment variable caused it. Both shipped workflows declare JUDGE, so only `--workflow <path>` workflows are affected — hence medium, not high. Suggested fix: apply the env-sourced override only to vars the resolved workflow declares (an explicit --judge-model/--judge-effort flag should still reach Resolve so a real conflict is reported), mirroring the calibration carve-out. The unit test at internal/fsm/cli/judgeoverride_test.go:113-117 asserts the injecting behaviour on a vars map with no JUDGE key, so it pins the defect rather than catching it.

findings.note: docs/fsm/sdlc-loop-example.md contradicts itself on the scenario path and the headline command does not run. Line 3 names the scenario `testdata/fsm/scenarios/sdlc-loop/happy`, but line 8 passes `--mock-ai scenarios/sdlc-loop/happy`. --mock-ai joins a relative path against the repo root (internal/fsm/cli/run.go:268-272), so copy-pasting the documented command from the repo root fails immediately with ERR_MOCK_INVALID (verified against the built binary: "open <root>/scenarios/sdlc-loop/happy/judge.yaml: no such file or directory"). Since the document's whole claim is that it shows the suite's own invocation, the first line a reader tries should work. Fix: `--mock-ai testdata/fsm/scenarios/sdlc-loop/happy`.

findings.note: The doc comment on applyJudgeOverride states an invariant the code does not always hold: "The map is copied: the caller's parsed vars are not a place to leave side effects." When neither the flag nor the env is set, applyJudgeOverrideFor returns the caller's own map by reference (wiring.go:276-278). Nothing mutates the result today (workflow.Resolve builds a fresh `effective` map and machine.Init only reads o.Vars), so this is not a live bug, but a caller trusting the comment and mutating the returned map would corrupt the parsed flags. Either copy unconditionally or narrow the comment to "copied when an override applies" — the existing test at judgeoverride_test.go:66-70 already asserts the no-copy path.

evidence.note: "The map is copied: the caller's parsed vars are not a place to leave side effects." vs the early `return vars` at wiring.go:277.

findings.note: ctxDeps.nonce panics on a Rand failure with an errs.E(CodeInternal) value, but nothing recovers it: grep for `recover()` across the repo hits only internal/fsm/cli/cli_test.go:626, and cmd/metareview/main.go has no recover. So the one code path that builds a structured ERR_INTERNAL error can never emit it as an envelope — the process dies with a Go panic and a stack trace on stderr, breaking the "every failure is a JSON envelope" contract the rest of the CLI keeps. Practically unreachable (crypto/rand does not fail on the supported platforms) and the seam is only injectable in tests, hence low. If the panic is deliberate, a top-level recover in main that renders the errs.E as an ERROR envelope would close the gap.

evidence.note: panic(errs.E(CodeInternal, "crypto/rand failed: "+err.Error())) with no recover anywhere in cmd/metareview/main.go.

findings.note: Two small test-hygiene gaps in the new internal/fsm/machine/handoffs_test.go. (1) Line 42 does `unlock2, _ := h.store.Lock(m.runID)` and calls unlock2() at line 46 — if Lock ever returned an error, unlock2 is nil and the test panics with a nil func call instead of reporting the real failure; the sibling Lock at line 22 is checked, so this is an inconsistency, not a style preference. (2) The comment at line 194 ("the machine's own work continues: the next index for judge@0 is 3") asserts nothing about the index: the following check is only `r.Seq == 0`. Either assert the index the comment names or drop the claim, otherwise the comment documents behaviour no test protects.
